governingStatute: Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015 read with Section 133 of Companies Act, 2013, IFRS 3, and US GAAP FASB ASC Topic 805
statutorySection: Ind AS 103 (Business Combinations) converged with IFRS 3 and aligned with US GAAP ASC 805
title: Business Combinations & Purchase Price Allocation (Acquisition Method, Identifiable Net Assets, Goodwill vs Capital Reserve, and Contingent Consideration)

effectivePeriod.annualReset: Acquisition date purchase price allocation with 1-year measurement period; annual goodwill impairment test under Ind AS 36
effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Mandatory accounting standard notified via MCA G.S.R. 111(E) effective FY 2015-16 onwards.

plainTextSummary: Under Ind AS 103 (converged with IFRS 3 and aligned with US GAAP ASC Topic 805), an entity accounts for each business combination by applying the acquisition method. The acquisition method requires: (1) identifying the acquirer; (2) determining the acquisition date (the date on which the acquirer obtains control of the acquiree); (3) recognizing and measuring the identifiable assets acquired, the liabilities assumed, and any non-controlling interest (NCI) in the acquiree at their acquisition-date fair values; and (4) recognizing and measuring goodwill or a gain from a bargain purchase. Identifiable assets include separately recognized intangible assets (such as customer relationships, brand names, software, and patents) regardless of whether they were recognized by the acquiree prior to acquisition, with corresponding deferred tax liabilities recognized under Ind AS 12 for the fair value step-up. Consideration transferred is measured at acquisition-date fair value, including cash, fair value of equity instruments issued, and the fair value of contingent consideration (earnouts). Non-controlling interest is measured either at fair value or at the NCI's proportionate share of the acquiree's identifiable net assets. If the aggregate of consideration transferred, NCI, and pre-existing equity interest exceeds the net acquisition-date fair value of identifiable assets and liabilities, the excess is recognized as Goodwill (tested annually for impairment under Ind AS 36; amortization is prohibited). Conversely, if the net identifiable assets exceed the acquisition basis, the excess represents a Bargain Purchase Gain; after a mandatory reassessment of all acquired assets and liabilities, the gain is recognized directly in Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) and accumulated in Equity as Capital Reserve. Acquisition-related costs (such as finder's fees, legal, accounting, valuation, and advisory fees) are expensed in the periods in which the costs are incurred and must not be capitalized into goodwill.

requiredDocumentChecklist: Executed Business Transfer Agreement (BTA), Share Purchase Agreement (SPA), or Scheme of Amalgamation sanctioned by NCLT
Independent Registered Valuer (RV) Purchase Price Allocation (PPA) report valuing tangible and intangible assets
Schedule of separately identifiable intangible assets (customer lists, software, trademarks, technology)
Contingent consideration valuation model, probability-weighted milestone matrix, and discount rate documentation
Deferred tax reconciliation statement detailing temporary differences arising from fair value step-ups under Ind AS 12
Board resolution and shareholder approvals authorizing consideration structure and acquisition terms
